....Respondents Date of institution of the petition : 18.12.2012 Date of final Arguments : 15.03.2023
Date of Decision : 15.03.2023 Appearance (s) :Shri Narender Singh, Ld. Counsel for the Petitioner
Shri S.S. Mitttal, Ld. Counsel for R1/Union of India.
Ms. Renu Gupta, Ld. Counsel for R2/Dda.

Shri Tejpal Shokeen, ld. Counsel for R3/ Dsidc Shri Parveen, Sr. Asst. for Lac (Nw).
Lac no. 93 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/Dc(Nw)) Baleshwar v. Union of India Page no. 1 of 10
Notification U/S 4 of Land Acquisition Act F.11(19)/2001/L&B/La/20112 dt. 21.03.2003
Notification U/s 6 of Land Acquisition Act F.11 (21)/2004/L&B/La/28049 dt. 18.03.2004
Reference Petition Under Section 18 Of The Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
J U D G M E N T

/ AWAR D (Under Section 26 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894)
1.

This is a reference petition u/s 18 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act"), filed by the petitioner mentioned aforesaid for enhancement of compensation awarded by the Land Acquisition Collector (NorthWest) (hereinafter called 'the LAC') for acquisition of their land for public purpose.
The petition was filed before the LAC and referred to by the Collector for determination of the court.

2. The brief factual matrix leading to the present petition is that the Government vide notification bearing No. F.11(19)/2001/L&B/LA/20112 dt. 21.03.2003 issued by the Lt. Governor of Delhi under Section 4 of the Act

, intended to acquire about 907 Bigha 09 biswas of land with its specification mentioned in the notification for public purpose namely 'Rohini Residential Scheme' under the "Planned Development of Delhi".

Sh. Baleshwar vs Union Of India on 15 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98567559/
1 3.
The Government vide consequent declaration/notification No. F.11 (21)/2004/L&B/LA/28049 dated 18.03.2004 issued pursuant thereto LAC no. 93 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW))

Baleshwar v. Union of India Page no. 2 of 10 under Section 6 of the Act, 907 Bigha 9 Biswas land (as detailed in the statement under Section 19 of the Act), acquired situated in the revenue estate of village Rani Khera, Delhi.

The LAC (N/W) after completing all the requisite formalities as provided under the Act, announced the Award bearing no.08 of 200506 dated 12.07.2005 u/s 11 of the Act in respect of 907 bighas 09 biswas out of the aforesaid said land and awarded a compensation at the uniform rate of Rs.15,70,000/ per acre (or Rs. 3,27,083.33/ per bigha) for the entire land in addition to other statutory benefits and interests besides liquidated cost for trees, tubewell and borings.

4. It is stated that the petitioner is the cobhumidhar and is in possession of land measuring 8 bighas and 12 biswas, in khasra no. 47/3 (4 16), 47/8 (316) situated in the revenue estate of Village Rani Khera, Delhi (in short, the said land).
5.
It is stated that the petitioner is owner and in possession of the said land, which is free from all encumbrances like mortgages, charges, lien.
6. It is stated that the petitioner is entitled to receive the compensation amount of the actual prevailing market value of the said land.

The ld. LAC has failed in assessing the price of the said land and the said award has been passed amount of which is inadequate, arbitrary, unjust, LAC no. 93 /
2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Baleshwar v. Union of India Page no. 3 of 10 illusionary without any reasonable aspects and the Award is not acceptable to the petitioner.
7.
It is submitted that the said award has been passed with grave error and the ld. LAC has failed to appreciate the law on the points involved.

The assessment of market value of the said land has been guided by the notions and assumptions, rather reality of the facts points towards a steady rise in the value of the said land owing to largescale of purchase of land by private builders, business houses,
industrialists on a very cumulative rates during the past several years, therefore, the market value of the said land is higher than the value assessed by the ld. LAC 8.
The ld. LAC has ignored the facts that the said land is surrounded with the land of much higher rates.
He has also ignored the facts that the said land was the only source of income of the petitioner and after acquisition of the said land, the petitioner has become unemployed.
The ld. LAC has also ignored the fact that the said land is very fertile and potential and commercial crops were sown by the petitioner and was the only source of income of the petitioner.

The principles of calculation of the market value land prevailing in village Rani Khera and nearby villages/residential areas are not taken into consideration and price of land in vicinity of the said land are much higher at the time of acquisition of the said land.

The assessment of the market value of the said land has been done arbitrarily by ignoring the principle of natural justice and if necessary inquiry would have LAC no.
93 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW))
Baleshwar v. Union of India Page no. 4 of 10 been done, the market value of the said land was Rs. 10,000/ per square yards.

Sh. Baleshwar vs Union Of India on 15 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98567559/
2 9.

It is submitted that the ld. LAC has totally ignored the facts that the said land is adjacent to the main road which is having well developed farmhouses, main roads and railway line is also passing in the vicinity of th said land.
The said land is also very fertile land having great potentiality and substantial value.

The learned LAC has also ignored the facts that all the basic facilities like electricity, water, telephone, banks, post offices, schools, hospital, food supplies office, roads are present in the village Rani Khera.

The ld. LAC has ignored the fact that the said land has great potential and situational value in as much as on the other side of the land there is a residential colonies which also increases the market value of the said land, and the said land is now cannot be called as agriculture land, however, ld. LAC has failed to appreciate the said fact.

It is submitted that by way of the present petition, the petitioner has sought the increase in market value of the said land @ Rs. 10,000 per square yards and the solatium @ 30% along with other additional amounts from the date of notification along with interest.

10. Written statement has been filed on behalf of respondent no.1/Union of India and, it is, inter alia, submitted that the petition is not maintainable as the petitioner failed to furnish any evidence in respect thereof.

The ld. LAC has already assessed the market value of the said LAC no. 93 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Baleshwar v. Union of India Page no. 5 of 10 land, taking into consideration the prevailing market rates at the time of the passing of the notification under Section 4 of the Act.

The possession of the said land as detailed under Section 19 of the said Act have been taken by ld. LAC on 15.12.2005, and after taking the possession of the said land the same has been handed over to DDA, therefore, DDA is also necessary and proper party to the present petition.
It is stated that the correctness of khasra number, their area and the extent of their share are admitted only to the extent as specified by the LAC in the statement under section 19 of the Act.

All the other contents mentioned in the present in the present petition are denied in toto and and it has been submitted that the reference filed by the petitioner is misconceived and as such liable to be dismissed.

11. Written statement has been filed on behalf of respondent no.2/DDA and, inter alia, it is submitted that the said land has been taken over by the DDA and as per Kabza karwahi report dated 29.11.2007 the said land has been taken back by the L&B department from DDA and handed over to DSIDC.
It is also written in Kabza Karwahi that the compensation/alternative allotment/enhanced compensation will be paid by DSIDC.
It is submitted that as the DDA is not the beneficiary of the said land, therefore, they are not liable to pay any compensation.
It is prayed that the reference petition filed by the petitioner is liable to be dismissed with cost.
LAC no. 93 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Baleshwar v. Union of India Page no. 6 of 10 12.
On the basis of pleadings of the parties and documents filed on record, the following issues were framed by the court on 17.01.2015 :  ISSUES 1.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for enhancement in compensation, if yes, then to what extent ?
OPP 2. Relief.

Sh. Baleshwar vs Union Of India on 15 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98567559/
3 13.

Matter was listed for recording of petitioner's evidence and counsel for the petitioner adopted the evidence led in the leading case in terms of the order dated 20.08.2022 passed by ld. pre decessor of this court.
14. Sh. Vinay Kumar, ld.

Counsel for the respondent no.1 has tendered on the Award which is Ex.
R1W1/A.
The evidence of respondent no.1 has been relied upon by ld.
Counsel for respondent no.2 DDA.
Counsel for the petitioner as well as ld.
Counsel for the respondents have submitted that they are relying upon the upon the evidence led by them in case bearing LAC no. 390 of 2016 Mukhtyar Singh v. Union of India, Village Rani Khera.

entities.text: Mukhtyar Singh v. Union of India, Village Rani Khera
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, no specific separate additional evidence for enhancement of compensation has been led.

16. I have heard the Ld. Counsels for the parties and have perused the entire record including the documents and the evidence led by the LAC no. 93 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW))
Baleshwar v. Union of India Page no. 7 of 10 parties.
I have given a thoughtful consideration to the same.

My issue wise findings and determination are as under:  WHETHER THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLED FOR ENHANCEMENT IN COMPENSATION, IF YES, THEN TO WHAT EXTENT ?
OPP 17.
The onus of proving the aforesaid issue is on the petitioner.
It is settled proposition of law that the onus to prove the market value of the said land or inadequacy of compensation awarded by LAC is always upon the petitioner.

The aforesaid proposition of law has been authoritatively held by our Hon'ble Supreme Court in State of UP & Anr. v. Rajender Singh, AIR 1996 SC 1564 as under:
"The onus is on the petitioners to prove that their lands are capable of fetching higher compensation then what has been determined by the LAC and that he is entitled for enhanced compensation".
18.

entities.text: State of UP & Anr. v. Rajender Singh, AIR 1996 SC 1564
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: To prove its case, the petitioner, through his counsel have adopted the evidence led in case Mukhtyar Singh (supra).
During the course of arguments, he has relied upon the judgment passed in the aforementioned case on 06.01.2023 and Ld.
Counsel for the petitioner has argued that the petitioner may also be awarded compensation as awarded to the petitioners in the aforementioned case.
LAC no. 93 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Baleshwar v. Union of India Page no. 8 of 10 19.
Even, the respondents have also relied upon the evidence led by the respondents in the aforementioned case and no separate evidence has been led by them in the present case.

20. Since the fair market value of the land situated in village Rani Khera are covered by the award in question has already been determined by this court, this court has no reason or evidence to deviate therefrom.
In view of the aforesaid discussion, this court also determines the same enhanced market value in the present case, in so far as the acquisition of the land of petitioner is concerned.

Sh. Baleshwar vs Union Of India on 15 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98567559/
4 21.

In the Mukhtyar Singh (supra), this court had adjudicated the market value of land of village Rani Kera acquired through Award No.08 of 200506 dated 12.07.2005 as Rs. 19,73,583/ per acre i.e. an enhancement of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre has been given.
There is no evidence on record to gather that the land of the petitioners herein was in any way inferior to the land involved in Mukhtyar Singh (supra).
The petitioner is accordingly entitled to the same compensation for his land as was awarded in Mukhtyar Singh (supra).
This court adjudicate the market value of land of the petitioners as Rs.19,73,583/ per acre thereby giving an enhancement of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre.
22. The petitioner has not led any evidence with respect to alleged damages of the growing crops and structures or other claims.

Therefore, the LAC no. 93 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW))
Baleshwar v. Union of India Page no. 9 of 10 petitioners shall not be entitled to any damages on the aforesaid counts.
This issue is decided accordingly in favour of the petitioner RELIEF 23.

In view of the findings on Issue No.1, the petitioner is granted the following reliefs:
(i) Fair Market value of land of petitioners as mentioned in the revised statement u/s 19 of the Act @
Rs.19,73,583/ per acre.
An of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre is accordingly accorded.

(ii) Additional amount @ 12% (in terms of Section 23(1A) of the Act).
(iii) Solatium @ 30% on the enhanced compensation ( in terms of S.23 (2) of the Act).
(iv) Interest @ 9% per annum for the first year and 15% per annum for the subsequent year till the payment of enhanced compensation by LAC is made (in terms of Section 28 of the Act).
24.
Reference petition is accordingly, answered with parties to bear their own respective costs.
Decree sheet be drawn accordingly.
File be consigned to record room after due compliance.
ANNOUNCED IN THE OPEN COURT ON 15th DAY OF MARCH, 2023.
